changes.before: Create the hero with name, health, and equipment fields.
changes.after: Group a character's details in an object and change just its health.

before: An object groups related values under property names. A property pairs a name with a value. Write braces `{}` around an object, a colon `:` between each property name and value, and commas between properties. One character object can hold text for its name, a number for its health, and an array for its equipment.

Dot notation reads a named property. `character.health` means get the health property of character. Add `= 9` to replace that property's value. This assignment targets one property; it does not replace the whole object. To read an item inside an array property, combine dot notation with an index, such as `character.equipment[0]`.

Objects are mutable, which means their contents can change. Declaring the variable with `const` keeps the name attached to this object; it does not freeze the properties. `character.health = 9;` is allowed. Trying to assign a different whole object to `character` is not allowed after a const declaration. These are different operations.

Property spelling matters just like variable spelling. `health` and `Health` refer to different properties. Reading an absent property normally gives `undefined`. Keep related information in one object but be precise about which field an instruction changes. If you wanted subtraction, you would write an expression such as `character.health = character.health - 3;`, which reads the current value before assigning the new one.

In the exercise, hero already contains Mira, health 10, and lantern equipment. Assign 7 to hero's health property, then read the existing name and equipment. The checks compare all three results so you can see that the targeted update worked. Think of the colon as pairing a property during creation and the equals sign as assigning a value afterward.
after:
An object groups related values under names called properties. A character can have a name, health, and equipment.

Braces surround the object. A colon pairs each property with its value, and commas separate the properties.

`character.health` reads the health property. `character.health = 9` assigns it a new value.

To read an item in an array property, use both the dot and an index: `character.equipment[0]`.

Objects are mutable: their contents can change. `const` keeps the name pointing to this object, but its properties can still change.

Updating `character.health` is allowed. Assigning a different whole object to this `const` name is not.

Property names must be spelled exactly. `health` and `Health` are different. A missing property normally gives `undefined`.

To subtract from the old health, read it in the calculation: `character.health = character.health - 3`.

The supplied `hero` already has the name Mira, health 10, and a lantern. Assign 7 to `hero.health`, then read the other properties too.

A colon pairs a property with a value when making the object. `=` assigns a value afterward.
